title: Uniform CPA Examination (CPA Evolution)
source: AICPA/NASBA Uniform CPA Examination Blueprints (CPA Evolution 2024+)
summary: The US CPA Evolution licensure model features 3 mandatory Core exams (AUD, FAR, REG) plus 1 candidate-selected Discipline (BAR, ISC, or TCP), governed by the 30-month rolling credit window and the 4 Es of licensure.

core-isc.name: Information Systems & Controls (ISC) Discipline Track
core-isc.blurb: Focuses on enterprise IT governance, internal controls, cybersecurity assurance, data management, and SOC attestation reporting.

stages.title: Stage 1: Eligibility & Notice to Schedule (NTS)
stages.subtitle: 120 credit hour board application, credential evaluation, and Prometric NTS

nodes.name: 120 Semester Hours & State Board Approval
nodes.description: Meet jurisdictional prerequisite of at least 120 semester hours (including required accounting and business credits) and receive authorization from your State Board of Accountancy.
topics: 120 Credit Hours Prerequisite
Accounting & Business Subject Minimums
State Board Eligibility Review

nodes.name: NASBA Notice to Schedule (NTS) Issuance
nodes.description: Receive your NASBA Notice to Schedule (NTS) valid for 6 months, and book computer-based exam appointments at Prometric testing centers.
topics: NASBA Portal Registration
NTS Validity Window
Prometric Scheduling

stages.title: Stage 2: The Mandatory CPA Core (12 Hours CBT · 30-Month Window)
stages.subtitle: Mandatory 3 Core Exams required of all CPA candidates across 55 jurisdictions

nodes.name: Auditing and Attestation (AUD)
nodes.description: Ethics, professional responsibilities, assessing risk and developing a planned response, performing procedures, obtaining evidence, and forming conclusions/reporting under AICPA, PCAOB, and IAASB standards.
topics: Ethics, Professional Responsibilities & General Principles (15-25%)
Assessing Risk and Developing a Planned Response (25-35%)
Performing Further Procedures and Obtaining Evidence (30-40%)
Forming Conclusions and Reporting: Opinions, Reviews, Compilations & SOC (10-20%)
learningOutcomes: Evaluate audit risks and design substantive and internal control audit procedures
Draft and evaluate unmodified, qualified, adverse, and disclaimer audit opinions
checklists: Score 75 or higher on scaled 0-99 grading scale
Subject to the 30-month rolling credit expiration window upon passing

nodes.name: Financial Accounting and Reporting (FAR)
nodes.description: Financial reporting framework, standard-setting, financial statement presentation, balance sheet accounts, transactions (revenue recognition, leases, taxes), and state/local government accounting.
topics: Financial Reporting Framework: FASB Standard Setting & Financial Statements (25-35%)
Select Balance Sheet Accounts: Inventory, Leases, PPE, Debt & Equity (35-45%)
Select Transactions: Revenue Recognition (ASC 606), Income Taxes & Contingencies (20-30%)
State and Local Government Accounting: Modified Accrual & Fund Accounting (5-15%)
learningOutcomes: Prepare complex corporate balance sheets, multi-step income statements, and cash flows
Execute fund accounting and government-wide financial reconciliations under GASB
checklists: Score 75 or higher on scaled 0-99 grading scale
Subject to the 30-month rolling credit window

nodes.name: Taxation and Regulation (REG)
nodes.description: Ethics, professional responsibilities, federal tax procedures, business law, federal taxation of property transactions, individuals, and corporate entities under the Internal Revenue Code (IRC).
topics: Ethics, Professional Responsibilities & Federal Tax Procedures (10-20%)
Business Law: Agency, Contracts, UCC, Debtor-Creditor & Business Structure (10-20%)
Federal Taxation of Property Transactions: Basis, Gain/Loss & Like-Kind (12-22%)
Federal Taxation of Individuals: Gross Income, Deductions & Credits (22-32%)
Federal Taxation of Entities: C Corps, S Corps, Partnerships & Trusts (28-38%)
learningOutcomes: Calculate basis adjustments and tax liabilities for corporations, S corporations, and partnerships
Analyze Circular 230 ethical standards and preparer penalty provisions
checklists: Score 75 or higher on scaled 0-99 grading scale
Subject to the 30-month rolling credit window

stages.title: Stage 3: Discipline Specialization (ISC)
stages.subtitle: 4 Hours CBT: 82 MCQs + 6 Task-Based Simulations (60% / 40% split)

nodes.name: Information Systems and Controls (ISC)
nodes.description: Information systems and controls discipline examining IT governance, internal controls, system availability, confidential data management, and SOC 1/2/3 attestation engagements.
topics: Information Systems and Data Management: Architecture & Cloud Virtualization (35-45%)
Security, Confidentiality, and Privacy: IAM, Zero Trust, Incident Response & HIPAA/GDPR (35-45%)
Considerations for System and Organization Controls (SOC) Engagements (15-25%)
learningOutcomes: Plan and execute SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2 attestation engagements
Audit enterprise identity architectures, multi-factor authentication, and data privacy controls

stages.title: Stage 4: Licensure & The 4 Es
stages.subtitle: 150 credit hours, 1-2 years experience, ethics exam, and State Board license

nodes.name: 150 Semester Hour Education Requirement
nodes.description: Satisfy the mandatory 150-semester-hour education requirement (equivalent to a Master's degree or post-graduate certificate) with specified accounting and business coursework.
topics: 150 Semester Hours Total
Upper-Level Accounting Credits
Business & Ethics Credits

nodes.name: 1 to 2 Years Verified Professional Accounting Experience
nodes.description: Complete 1 to 2 years of qualifying professional experience in public accounting, private corporate accounting, internal audit, or government, verified by an active CPA licensee.
topics: Public Accounting or Industry Experience
Active CPA Verifier Sign-Off

nodes.name: State Board Ethics Examination
nodes.description: Pass the AICPA Comprehensive Professional Ethics Examination (or specific state-mandated ethics examination) with a minimum score of 90%.
topics: AICPA Code of Professional Conduct
Independence Rules (Rule 101)
Confidentiality & Fiduciary Duties
